title: First-byte equalizer hotfix for cross-deployment TTFT and tokens/sec instability
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A set of customer escalations (Hosted + Dedicated + Private clusters) surfaced an abrupt divergence in first-byte latency (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec for short prompt workloads after a scheduler prefetch tuning landed in runtime-1.22. Symptoms are most pronounced for quantized and short-context models: TTFT increased by up to 2.4x and tokens/sec dropped ~25-35% for affected customers during peak bursts.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed via traces):
- The new prefetch/coalescer heuristic increased the prefetch window for long-session models which inadvertently increased scheduler hold times for small, low-token-rate requests.
- Small/short requests were queued behind prefetch-heavy fanout tasks; KV-cache warmup and kernel selection delays amplified first-byte skew across deployments.
- Private clusters with tighter capacity and Dedicated pools with asymmetric instance types exhibited more severe degradation due to reduced multiplexing.

Mitigation implemented (hotfix):
- Introduced a temporary scheduler config 'first_byte_equalizer=true' that biases scheduling priority towards small/initial-token requests for the first N ms of a request's lifecycle and caps prefetch window on quantized models.
- Patch added an opt-in flag at route-level and global runtime default; no model binary changes.
- Canary rollout initiated for 5% of Hosted, 10% of a Dedicated pool, and one Private customer cluster.

Immediate results:
- Canary telemetry shows TTFT improvement: median TTFT dropped from 180ms to 85ms for short prompts; p95 improved by ~300ms on canary hosts.
- Tokens/sec on affected microbenchmarks recovered to within 8% of baseline.

Rollback plan: 
- If canary exhibits token-rate regressions or increased overall latency, revert flag to false and re-enable previous prefetch parameters (fast rollback path implemented in orchestration).

Testing & validation: 
- Synthetic harness: ran 10k short-prompt QPS across 3 model families (gpt-7b-int8, redwood-3b-fp16, open-8k-quant) with and without flag.
- End-to-end smoke on Dedicated: customer sandbox replay of traces for MiraPay and EduSync.
- Added new unit tests for scheduler priority ordering and an integration test that asserts no >1.5x spike in median TTFT under burst load.

Customer communication & follow-ups: 
- Notified impacted customers (MiraPay, EduSync, HealthVault) with initial root-cause and canary plan. Support engineers provided mitigations and prioritized dedicated-channel monitoring.
- Post-deployment follow-up: scheduled customer check-ins 2026-03-17 and 2026-03-21.

Next steps / TODOs (post-hotfix):
- Promote to 25%/50%/100% rollout if canary remains stable (target completion 2026-03-18).
- Author permanent scheduling change proposal (ENG PR + design doc) to replace the temporary flag with a latency-aware scheduler that considers per-request priming cost.
- Create a regression test in perf-ci that replays a representative short-prompt workload nightly.
- Enhance telemetry: add token-rate and TTFT split by model family + deployment type to the runtime dashboard and an alert for >1.5x TTFT deviation.
- Document runbook steps for on-call (how to toggle flag, key dashboards, when to contact runtime-oncall).

Artifacts & links: 
- GH patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4872 (hotfix branch)
- Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary/ENG-830211
- Internal design stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/first-byte-equalizer

Notes: 
- This ticket is intentionally scoped to ship a fast, low-risk runtime config change. A separate follow-up ticket will design the long-term scheduler rework with deeper perf regressions tests and kernel selection improvements.
